goal: The harness performs summarize-restart recovery -- finalizing an over-ratio continuing attempt RECOVERED, emitting harness.context_recovery, and scheduling a fresh attempt carrying the summarizer's `# Recovery handoff` -- bounded by max_context_recoveries and preempted by completion/loop-guard.

references: src/flywheel/harness.py:2493 -- loop_guard.observe verdict check then the intent==CONTINUE decision; the recovery trigger evaluates immediately AFTER the loop-guard check so loop-guard precedes recovery (FR-6)
src/flywheel/harness.py:2452 -- usage_breakdown / usage_payload already built for harness.iteration_completed; occupancy = input + cache-read + cache-creation tokens (no new SDK plumbing, spec 00009)
src/flywheel/harness.py:1489 -- the FAILED_VALIDATION/INTERNAL_ERROR retry arm (RetryScheduled -> READY); recovery reuses this RetryScheduled->AttemptStarted machinery to schedule the fresh attempt
src/flywheel/harness.py:2638 -- _finalize_attempt usage; finalize the recovered attempt with Outcome.RECOVERED
src/flywheel/harness.py:2578 -- RubricJudgeError handling; mirror this to route a raised summarizer through INTERNAL_ERROR
constraints: Precedence (FR-6): completion-claim > loop-guard STUCK/THRASH > recovery. Recovery fires ONLY for a validly-continuing iteration (intent=continue, no loop-guard verdict, no completion claim). Order the recovery check after the existing loop_guard.observe break.
FR-2: when context_window_tokens is None, compute no occupancy and never recover -- the existing harness suite must pass unchanged.
Occupancy is the latest iteration's input-side tokens (input + cache-read + cache-creation) from usage_payload, NOT a summed running counter (Decisions Log).

FR-4: at most max_context_recoveries recoveries per run_task call via an in-process counter; once exhausted, an over-ratio iteration does NOT recover and the loop follows its normal termination path. The recovery budget is independent of max_retries.
FR-3: invoke the summarizer via config.recovery_summarizer_invoke (the injected seam), thread its handoff into the next attempt's IterationInputs so prompt.py renders `# Recovery handoff`.

FR-5: emit one harness.context_recovery event carrying iteration, attempt_number, occupancy tokens, context_window_tokens, context_recovery_trigger_ratio, recoveries_used, recoveries_remaining, and a summary digest -- ordered BEFORE the recovery attempt's AttemptStarted.

Error Handling: a summarizer raise/timeout aborts recovery for that iteration and routes through INTERNAL_ERROR (same class as a failed rubric judge) -- never silently restart with an empty handoff. An iteration with no usage data is treated as below-ratio (no recovery, no event).
Persist RECOVERED into the existing attempts.outcome column -- no ADD COLUMN, no new store Protocol method, no schema change.
Remove the 'context-recovery policy' entry from _DEFERRED_LOOP_SUBSYSTEMS (harness.py:158) in this commit.
Commit with a Conventional Commits message (feat: ...) before emitting intent=verify.
non_goals: No compact/fork action and no action-selection policy -- summarize-restart only (spec Out of Scope).
No recover control verb / CONTROL_COMMAND_*; no intra-iteration mid-turn recovery; no cross-process budget persistence.
Do not add a typed events.py dataclass -- use the kind-string harness.context_recovery via _emit.
edge_cases: Over-ratio on the very first iteration -> first attempt finalizes RECOVERED, second attempt is the working attempt.
Budget exhausted but still over-ratio -> no recovery, normal termination, no harness.context_recovery event.
max_iterations_per_attempt=1 + a single over-ratio iteration -> recovery applies between attempts.
Recovery and validation-retry budgets are independent (max_context_recoveries vs max_retries).
Capacity set but ratio never crossed -> feature inert, identical to disabled.

graders.run: uv run python -c "from flywheel.harness import _DEFERRED_LOOP_SUBSYSTEMS as d; assert 'context-recovery policy' not in d"
